text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newspaper editorial says the government should deal with armed bands of supporters of former President Sali Berisha alleged to be trying to organise a rebellion in the north.
- The new government of Socialist leader Fatos Nano won a vote of confidence and will visit Italy to meet international experts on July 31 to discuss Albania's reconstruction.
- Albania's wheat production this year is expected to be 400,000 tonnes, higher than last year but will not bring much improvement for farmers.
- The finance ministry has started a drive against smuggling in the country and plans to strengthen customs controls.
- Ali Ukaj, one of the daily's reporters, was found dead after being massacred at his apartment in Tirana.
- The population in Vlore is increasingly worried about the security situation after the early departure of the Italian multinational force from the town.

- The second stage of the soccer league, which was interrupted by violent unrest in January, will restart this weekend as police said they would have the security situation in the stadiums under control.
- Although Italy led the multinational force in Albania the new Socialist government favours Greece as a contact point with the rest of Europe.
- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos will visit Albania on August 5.

- Fatos Nano, leader of the Socialist party and new prime minister, on the anniversary of his arrest four years ago, called on Albanians from the former Democratic party regime to help rebuild the country together.

- Transparency of investment schemes is one of the priorities of the new government after thousands of Albanians lost their life savings in shady pyramid schemes. A new law is due to be presented to the parliament.
